lead: Bitcoin / BTC-USD — crypto spring after the January freeze
smaller: Peloton Interactive / PTON — the takeover pop meets the sceptics
Meta Platforms / FB — the falling knife that keeps falling
Exxon Mobil / XOM — the war hedge in a value wrapper
why_lead: Crypto had the broadest significant move on the card (BTC 43,840.29 USD, +18.64% over five days; ETH +17.13%; XRP +21.09% in one day, +37.63% over five; DOGE +20.65%) plus genuine retail-attention evidence published 7 February: The Independent on memecoins' dramatic rise [[n0944]], MoneySense's Shiba-vs-Dogecoin explainer [[n0938]], FTX's free-bitcoin Super Bowl promotion [[n0933]], and Al Jazeera's 'Crypto spring?' five-straight-days headline [[n0929]]. Relation to earlier retail notes: the 2022-02-07 edition ran the crypto bounce only as a secondary item through MicroStrategy (MSTR); this lead is a material update with newly published evidence ([[n0929]], [[n0944]], [[n0936]], [[n1785]]) and a different vehicle (Bitcoin and the memecoin spillover). The 2022-02-01 draft (GameStop, Netflix, Spotify, ARKK) did not cover crypto; the 2022-02-02 draft ran Solana only as an NFT-festival secondary item, and the 2022-02-04 draft ran Bitcoin only as a secondary 'faithful hold while Big Tech bleeds' item at 37,154.60 USD; neither covered the five-day rebound to 43,840.29 USD or the memecoin spillover, which rest on 7 February evidence. Independent review (chronology): headlines the 2022-02-07 MicroStrategy item had already used (Fundstrat's $200k forecast, Al Jazeera's 'past $40,000', CNBC's $320 million hack) were replaced with newer or not-yet-used evidence — a banking veteran's five cryptos in Business Insider [[n0923]], Reuters' 'bitcoin mimics stocks rally' [[n0635]] as the own-story test, and Futurism's NFT-collector crash warning [[n0922]] — so the lead's angle (five-day spring plus memecoin spillover) rests on evidence not used in the 2022-02-07 item.
why_smaller: Peloton: carried over from the 2022-02-07 secondary item with a material update — the rumoured premium became a completed +20.93% session to 29.75 USD, with new 7 February coverage from BBC [[n0766]], Sky News [[n0824]], Wedbush's Apple case [[n0801]] and CNBC's 'why a deal might not happen' [[n0823]]; kept secondary and focused on the premium-versus-results test rather than repeating the lottery framing. The Bloomberg regulatory-headache headline used on 2022-02-07 was dropped from this item.

Meta Platforms: brief carryover (155 words, secondary). Meta led on 2022-02-03 and 2022-02-04 (the 4 February lead already used the Berkshire market-value and Buffett 'ruled out buying' headlines) and was the foil on 2022-02-07, so the item was cut to a brief carryover that cites only post-crash 6–7 February catalysts — CNBC on a possible Facebook/Instagram shutdown in Europe [[n1279]], Thiel leaving the board [[n0789]], USA Today's 'cluttered and dated' young users [[n0739]] — and the further 7 February decline (-5.14% to 224.91 USD; -28.20% over five sessions).

Exxon Mobil: a distinct war-and-inflation hedge narrative built on newly published evidence — Biden's Nord Stream 2 pledge [[n1261]], strategists' $100 oil call in Reuters [[n1384]], the Macron–Putin de-escalation track [[n1277]] — with XOM +19.61% and XLE +13.76% over 20 sessions and Brent 92.69 USD/bbl. Relation to earlier notes: the 2022-02-02 draft ran Exxon as 'Big Oil pays you to wait' on the 1 February results/buyback, with the World Oil Permian headline as a break; this item acknowledges the buyback only as old news [[n1296]], uses Houston Public Media's Permian-expansion report [[n0652]] instead of the recycled World Oil headline, and makes the new geopolitical premium the catalyst, kept secondary.
considered_not_chosen: Robinhood Markets / HOOD (-8.37% on 7 February while crypto rose; Michael Lewis 'Vanguard more disruptive than Robinhood' [[n0760]]): interesting divergence but no own-date catalyst explaining the drop.
Snap / SNAP (-2.65% after the 58.82% day): the 2022-02-07 lead; no new catalyst, so not repeated.
Nvidia–Arm termination reports ([[n0819]], [[n1949]]): avoided because the formal termination is an 8 February event and these 7 February-stamped headlines may describe it after the cutoff.
Block / SQ (-5.57%, -15.93% over five sessions) and PayPal / PYPL (-29.39% over five sessions): drawdowns without fresh own-date catalysts in the window.
Digital World Acquisition / DWAC (+55.39% over 20 sessions): no own-date DWAC headline.
Netflix via Bill Ackman's stake ([[n0775]]): the 2022-02-01 draft already ran Netflix as 'follow the billionaires into the dip'.
